findings.title: UsernameForm calls a zero-argument isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() that does not exist; services module will not compile
findings.body: `authenticate` calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments. The only declaration in the repository is `protected boolean isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` at services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authentication/authenticators/browser/UsernamePasswordForm.java:160. A repository-wide text search finds no zero-argument overload, so javac rejects this call. The services module, and therefore the server and the testsuite, cannot build with this head commit. Fix: resolve together with the next finding by making the helper parameterless (`webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled()`) and keeping this call as written.
findings.originReason: The diff adds the call with no arguments.

verification.reason: The only declaration of isConditionalPasskeysEnabled is the one-argument version at UsernamePasswordForm.java:160. UsernameForm.java:47 calls it with no arguments, and grep finds no zero-argument overload anywhere, so the services module does not compile.

findings.title: Passkey conditional UI is no longer set up on the fresh login page (user == null)
findings.body: The helper at lines 160-162 returns `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled() && user != null`. Before this PR, `authenticate` filled the passkey form in the `else` branch (user not set), and `challenge(context, error, field)` filled it when `context.getUser() == null`. Both sites now call the helper with `context.getUser()`, so they fill only when a user is already set. On a fresh login page (no user) in a realm with passkeys enabled, `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.fillContextForm` is no longer called. That method sets ENABLE_WEBAUTHN_CONDITIONAL_UI, CHALLENGE and RP_ID (WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.java:42-45, WebAuthnAuthenticator.java:85-95), so the username autocomplete 'username webauthn' and the webauth form disappear from the primary login page, and passkey autofill stops. Password login still works, and nothing reports an error. The PR's own tests that keep the first-page expectations would fail on this head: PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.java:145-146, 195-196, 237-238, 358-360; PasskeysUsernameFormTest.java:183-185, 241-243; PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest.java:192-194, 250-252. Fix: drop the `&& user != null` condition from the helper at lines 160-162 so it is `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled()`. The user-set re-authentication case still fills, because both call sites are no longer gated on the user. This also resolves the compile error at UsernameForm.java:47.
findings.originReason: The diff replaces the old checks (fill in the user-null else branch; `context.getUser() == null` in challenge) with a helper that requires a user.

verification.reason: The helper at line 161 requires `user != null`. Both fill sites (lines 115 and 137) pass context.getUser(), so on the first login page, where there is no user, fillContextForm is never called. Before this change it was called exactly in the no-user case, so passkey conditional UI disappears from the primary login page.

findings.title: With passkeys enabled, re-authentication no longer skips the username page for users without a passkey
findings.body: The skip at lines 46-53 is now bypassed whenever passkeys are enabled in the realm, for every user who is already set, not only for users who have a passkey. A user without a passkey in a passkey-enabled realm therefore gets the username-only page (username hidden) and must submit it on every prompt=login. The PR body does not say this is intended. The new UsernameForm test (PasskeysUsernameFormTest.java:259-321) only covers a user who has a passkey. Question for the author: is the extra step intended for passkey-less users, or should the skip be bypassed only when the user has a passkey credential?

verification.reason: A zero-argument predicate on this class has no user or context to look at; the only per-realm inputs available are webauthnAuth and isPasskeysEnabled. So whatever form the fixed call takes, the re-authentication skip is bypassed for every set user in a passkey-enabled realm, including users with no passkey.

findings.title: reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey disables passkeys for the whole realm and does not test a passkey-less user in a passkey-enabled realm
findings.body: The test sets `setWebAuthnPolicyPasskeysEnabled(FALSE)` on the realm (line 282). The passkey-enabled branch of the new predicate and the UsernameForm skip branch are therefore never exercised for a user without a passkey, which is the case the name and the comment at line 304 describe. Either add a case with passkeys enabled and a passkey-less user, or rename the test to say the realm has passkeys disabled.

verification.reason: The test sets setWebAuthnPolicyPasskeysEnabled(FALSE) at line 282, so no test covers a passkey-less user in a passkey-enabled realm, which is the case the test name suggests.

contracts.action: Passkey (conditional UI) form setup on the UsernamePasswordForm login/re-auth page when authenticate() renders it
contracts.equivalent_path: Pre-PR: the else-branch of UsernamePasswordForm.authenticate (fill only when user is not set) and challenge(context, error, field) (fill when getUser()==null)
contracts.before_after: Before: fill ran only when no user was set and passkeys were enabled. After: fill runs only when a user is set and passkeys are enabled, so the no-user path no longer fills.
contracts.visible_effect: On a fresh login page in a passkeys-enabled realm, the passkey autofill (username autocomplete 'username webauthn', webauth form) is not rendered.
contracts.failure_mode: Silent. No error is shown; passkey login is not offered on the primary page; password login still works.

contracts.action: Passkey form setup on the 3-argument challenge(error, field) used by wrong-username and wrong-password renders
contracts.equivalent_path: Pre-PR: the same override with the condition context.getUser()==null
contracts.before_after: Before: passkey fill only when no user was set. After: passkey fill only when a user is set; the no-user case (first-page invalid username) loses passkey UI, and the re-auth wrong-password case gains it.
contracts.visible_effect: First-page invalid username: passkey UI disappears. Re-auth wrong password: passkey UI appears. PasswordForm (username-first flow) wrong password: passkey UI appears.
contracts.failure_mode: Silent. The password page shows passkey UI after a wrong password, and the first page loses it after a wrong username.

contracts.action: UsernameForm.authenticate skip of re-authentication when a user is set
contracts.equivalent_path: Pre-PR: the same method with `if (context.getUser() != null)` and the linked-brokers check, which calls context.success() to skip the form
contracts.before_after: Before: skip whenever a user is set and there are no other linked IdPs. After (as written): the call on line 47 does not compile. Intended: skip only when passkeys are disabled.
contracts.visible_effect: Build failure in the head commit. Once compiled, passkey-enabled realms show the username page on re-authentication for all users.
contracts.failure_mode: Compile error stops the server and testsuite from building.

contracts.action: Conditional-UI passkey error page calls the new helper that hides the username on re-authentication
contracts.equivalent_path: AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.badPasswordHandler (AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.java:218-224), which now calls the same helper
contracts.before_after: Before: a passkey error re-rendered the login form with the username field visible, even during re-authentication. After: when the USER_SET_BEFORE note is 'true', USERNAME_HIDDEN and REGISTRATION_DISABLED are set; otherwise nothing changes.
contracts.visible_effect: On a passkey failure during re-authentication, the username field is hidden, the same as for a password failure.
contracts.failure_mode: None. The helper only reads an auth note and sets form attributes; it does not throw.

contracts.action: Refactor of the password-error path to use the shared helper
contracts.equivalent_path: Pre-PR: the inline check in the same method, which called isUserAlreadySetBeforeUsernamePasswordAuth (AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.java:257-260)
contracts.before_after: Before and after read the same auth note with Boolean.parseBoolean and set the same two attributes. No behaviour change.

contracts.action: WebAuthnAuthenticator.fillContextForm now gates the authenticator list on shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators, overridden to false in the conditional UI
contracts.equivalent_path: Base shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators (user != null), which matches shouldDisplayAuthenticators at WebAuthnAuthenticator.java:147-149 and the pre-PR inline check
contracts.before_after: Before: with a user set in the conditional UI, the authenticator bean was built, and if it was empty fillContextForm returned null before setting USER_VERIFICATION and SHOULD_DISPLAY_AUTHENTICATORS. After: the conditional override returns false, so those attributes are always set and IS_USER_IDENTIFIED is false.
contracts.visible_effect: On the re-authentication page the passkey attributes are set and no authenticator list is shown. webauthn-authenticate.ftl guards the list with authenticators?? (lines 19-26), so no list renders.
contracts.failure_mode: None found. The template does not dereference authenticators when it is absent.

contracts.action: Passkey submission on the re-authentication page, now reachable with a user already set
contracts.equivalent_path: Fresh-login passkey submission through the same webauthnAuth.action call, using WebAuthnAuthenticator.action without a preset user (WebAuthnAuthenticator.java:187-197)
contracts.before_after: Before: the re-auth page had no passkey form, so a passkey submit with a preset user was not reached. After: the path is reached; when the userHandle differs from the preset user it returns WEBAUTHN_ERROR_DIFFERENT_USER (WebAuthnAuthenticator.java:204-211); otherwise it sets the user and succeeds (WebAuthnAuthenticator.java:258-265).
contracts.visible_effect: Successful passkey re-authentication, or an error page with a hidden username on failure.
contracts.failure_mode: setErrorResponse calls createErrorResponse, which the conditional override handles by calling the helper and fillContextForm (WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.java:48-57), so the user can retry on the same page.

contracts.action: Re-authentication skip for passkey-less users in a passkey-enabled realm (intended behaviour once UsernameForm compiles)
contracts.equivalent_path: Pre-PR: the same skip, which applies to every user who is already set
contracts.before_after: Before: the skip happened for all re-authenticating users. After (intended): the skip is disabled whenever passkeys are enabled, which applies to passkey-less users too.
contracts.visible_effect: Users without a passkey in passkey-enabled realms see the username page on prompt=login and must submit it.
contracts.failure_mode: The extra step is not a failure. Whether it is intended is open.
contracts.open_question: Should the skip be bypassed only for users who have a passkey credential, rather than for every user whenever realm passkeys are enabled?

summary: The PR does not compile and, once it does, it breaks passkey autofill on the primary login page. Two blockers. (1) UsernameForm.java:47 calls a zero-argument isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() that does not exist; the only declaration takes a UserModel (UsernamePasswordForm.java:160), so the services module will not build. (2) The helper's `user != null` condition (UsernamePasswordForm.java:160-162, used at :115 and :137) means fresh login pages (no user) never get the conditional UI, so 'username webauthn' autocomplete and the webauth form disappear. The pre-existing first-page assertions in the three passkey test classes would fail. Fix: make the helper parameterless (webauthnAuth != null && isPasskeysEnabled()), which also resolves the compile error. Consider-level questions: passkey-less users now lose the re-auth skip in passkey-enabled realms (UsernameForm.java:47); the password step after a wrong password now shows passkey UI (UsernamePasswordForm.java:137); and reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey disables realm passkeys, so it does not test the case its name describes (PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.java:279). The helper extraction in AuthenticatorUtils and the refactored badPasswordHandler are behaviour-preserving. The test-side additions (configureTestRealm at PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.java:73, the re-auth tests) are sound in intent. No ADR applies: docs/adr is not in the snapshot. I did not build or run anything; the compile error and the regression are established by reading the code.
